topic: Minecraft Java Edition (1.20.x) font + text rendering: metrics, advance-width table, shadow, formatting codes, and legally-safe lookalike fonts

facts.value: Derived from the IBM EGA 8x8 ROM character set; first used by Markus Persson in 2001 (Legend of the Chambered), then Minecraft Classic 0.0.2a
All rights reserved (Mojang/Microsoft); usable only under the Minecraft Usage Guidelines. NOT open source, NOT redistributable
128 x 128 pixels (measured directly on the 1.20.1 asset)
8 pixels (JSON `height` field default for bitmap providers; ascii.png omits it)

7 pixels (uppercase ink occupies rows 0-6 of the cell)
7 pixels (b d f h k l t and the i-dot reach row 0 - identical to cap height, no overshoot)
1 pixel below baseline (g p q y j , ; @ _ occupy row 7)
1 pixel, uniform, with zero exceptions across all 95 printable ASCII glyphs
1 pixel (9 px line height minus 8 px glyph box)
6 pixels (5 px ink + 1 px gap) - true for all A-Z, 0-9, and a-z except f i k l t
# $ % & + - / 0-9 = ? A-Z \ ^ _ and a-z minus f,i,k,l,t  (ink width 5 px)
+1 pixel X, +1 pixel Y (down and to the right) for bitmap glyphs

Shadow pass renders FIRST at (x+1, y+1), then the foreground pass at (x, y)
+1 pixel (glyph boldOffset = 1.0 px for bitmap glyphs, 0.5 px for unihex glyphs)
Glyph drawn twice: once at penX, once at penX + 1 pixel, same Y (no vertical duplication)
0.25 pixel horizontal offset per 1 pixel of vertical height = 2 pixels total lean across the 8 px glyph box
Applied symmetrically: top edge shifted +1 px, bottom edge shifted -1 px about the vertical midpoint

Underline and strikethrough use the current text color and are also emitted in the shadow pass, /4 color at +1,+1
Replaced each render by a uniformly random glyph whose INTEGER advance width equals the original glyph's integer advance width (rejection sampling)

notes:
## 1. Layout algorithm (implement exactly this)

```
penX = originX; penY = originY            // penY = TOP of the 8px glyph box
for each glyph g in run:
    if obfuscated: g = randomGlyphWithSameIntAdvance(g)
    adv = advanceOf(g)                     // = inkWidth(g) + 1
    if bold: adv += g.boldOffset           // 1.0 bitmap, 0.5 unihex
    drawGlyphQuad(g, penX, penY, italic)   // 8x8 cell, ink is LEFT-aligned in the cell
    if bold: drawGlyphQuad(g, penX + g.boldOffset, penY, italic)
    if strikethrough: fillRect(penX,   penY+3, penX+adv, penY+4)
    if underline:     fillRect(penX-1, penY+8, penX+adv, penY+9)
    penX += adv
// next line: penY += 9
```

`stringWidth(s) = sum(advance(c)) [+1 per char while bold]`. For pure ASCII at GUI scale 1 this is always an integer, so a clone can use integer math end-to-end.

## 2. Full ASCII advance table (pixels, includes the 1 px inter-glyph gap)

Verified by three independent sources that agree on every one of the 95 printable chars: (a) direct pixel measurement of the 1.20.1 `ascii.png` I downloaded and scanned, (b) the aerulion `BitmapGlyphInfo` ink-width dump (complete as of 1.19.3), (c) the Owen1212055/mc-fonts `minecraft_default.json` advance dump. `advance == ink + 1` held in all 95 cases.

| adv | chars |
|---|---|
| 2 | `!` `'` `,` `.` `:` `;` `i` `\|` |
| 3 | `` ` `` `l` |
| 4 | `SPACE` `"` `(` `)` `*` `I` `[` `]` `t` `{` `}` |
| 5 | `<` `>` `f` `k` |
| 6 | `#` `$` `%` `&` `+` `-` `/` `0`-`9` `=` `?` `A`-`Z` `\` `^` `_` `a`-`z` except f,i,k,l,t |
| 7 | `@` `~` |

Compact JS:
```js
const ADV = {' ': 4};
for (const c of "!',.:;i|")     ADV[c] = 2;
for (const c of "`l")           ADV[c] = 3;
for (const c of "\"()*I[]t{}")  ADV[c] = 4;
for (const c of "<>fk")         ADV[c] = 5;
for (const c of "@~")           ADV[c] = 7;
// every other printable ASCII: 6
```

`SPACE` is not derived from the texture in 1.20 â€” its cell is blank and the advance comes from a dedicated provider: `{"type":"space","advances":{" ":4,"\u200c":0}}`. Legacy versions hardcoded `charWidth[32] = 3 + 1 = 4`, same result.

## 3. Vertical metrics

- Cell 8x8. `height:8`, `ascent:7` => baseline sits 7 px below the cell top; exactly 1 px of the cell is below the baseline.
- Cap height **7 px** (rows 0-6). x-height **5 px** (rows 2-6). Ascenders **7 px**, i.e. no overshoot â€” `b d h k l t` top out at exactly cap height. Descender **1 px** (`g p q y` end on row 7). `j` uniquely spans rows 0-7.
- `@` is the only letterlike glyph sitting 1 px low: ink rows 1-7.
- `,` and `;` descend to row 7; `_` lives entirely on row 7; `.` is a single pixel on row 6.
- Line box 9 px => 1 px leading between 8 px glyph boxes. Wrapped-text height = `9 * lineCount` px.

## 4. Shadow

```js
const shadow = (argb & 0xFF000000) | ((argb & 0x00FCFCFC) >>> 2);
```
Masking with `0xFCFCFC` before `>>2` is exactly `floor(c/4)` per channel â€” the mask only clears bits the shift discards anyway, so `Math.floor(r/4)` etc. is equivalent. Alpha is copied unchanged.

Two full passes: shadow at `(x+1, y+1)` in shadow color, then foreground at `(x, y)`. Everything in the run is offset, including bold's second draw and the underline/strikethrough rects. Modern MC also nudges the shadow layer by 0.03 in Z; a 2D canvas clone just draws shadow first.

The wiki's "shadows are positioned 12.5% south-east" is 1/8 of the 8 px cell = 1 px.

Unihex (Unicode fallback) glyphs override both `shadowOffset` and `boldOffset` to **0.5 px**, because those glyphs are 16 px tall rendered into an 8 px box. This is why CJK text in Minecraft has a visibly tighter shadow than ASCII.

Edge case: if the caller's color has no bits set in `0xFC000000` (alpha < 4), vanilla forces opaque first: `if ((color & -67108864) == 0) color |= -16777216;`.

## 5. Formatting codes

- `Â§l` **bold** â€” advance `+boldOffset` (1 px bitmap / 0.5 px unihex); glyph drawn a second time at `x + boldOffset`, **same y**. Pure horizontal smear, no vertical duplication â€” which is why Minecraft bold reads as a 2px-stem font rather than a genuinely heavier design.
- `Â§o` **italic** â€” vertex shear only, no advance change, so bold+italic can visually collide with the next glyph. Legacy geometry: top vertices at `x+1`, bottom vertices at `x-1` across a 7.99 px tall quad. Modern equivalent: horizontal offset `= 1.0 - 0.25 * v` where `v` is the vertex's signed vertical coordinate => slope 0.25 px/px => **2 px total lean over the 8 px box, Â±1 px about the vertical centre**. Canvas: `ctx.transform(1, 0, -0.25, 1, 0.25 * (penY + 4), 0)`, or pre-shear the glyph atlas.
- `Â§n` **underline** â€” 1 px rect on line-box row 8 (immediately below the glyph box, inside the leading), and it deliberately extends **1 px to the left** of the pen (`x-1 .. x+adv`) so consecutive underlined chars form an unbroken rule with no seam.
- `Â§m` **strikethrough** â€” 1 px rect on line-box row 3 (`floor(9/2) = 4` is the *lower* edge, so the filled row index is 3). That lands at the vertical middle of the 5 px x-height.
- `Â§r` resets colour and all five style flags. In Java Edition applying any colour code `Â§0`-`Â§f` also clears bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/obfuscated.
- `Â§k` **obfuscated**:
  ```java
  do { j = random.nextInt(charWidth.length); }
  while ((int) charWidth[i] != (int) charWidth[j]);
  ```
  Rejection-sample any glyph whose **integer** advance equals the original's. Consequence: an `i` (2 px) only ever cycles through other 2 px glyphs, an `m` only through 6 px glyphs â€” total string width is stable and text never jitters horizontally. Re-rolled on every render call, so effectively re-randomised each frame (~60 Hz at 60 fps, not a fixed animation timer). Pre-1.13 the pool was restricted to the current 256-glyph page; 1.13+ it is all loaded glyphs of matching width.
  For a browser clone, prefer re-rolling on a fixed ~50 ms interval rather than per-rAF â€” per-frame at 120-144 Hz looks noisier than vanilla and burns CPU.

## 6. Legacy quad quirk (safe to skip)

1.8-era `renderDefaultChar` drew a **6.99 x 7.99 px** quad sampling `u in [cellX, cellX + 6.99]` â€” only 7 of the 8 columns of each cell, with the 0.01 epsilon to dodge texel bleed. Since max ink width is 6 px this is lossless. For a clone, blit the full 8x8 cell; ink is left- and top-aligned so trailing transparent columns cost nothing.

## 7. Legal framing

Do **not** ship Mojang's `ascii.png` â€” it is a copyrighted image asset inside a proprietary game, and "Minecraft"/"Mojang" are trademarks. But in the US typeface *designs* are not copyrightable (37 CFR 202.1(e)); only font *programs* (scalable outline/hinting code) are, and bitmap glyph data is generally treated as uncopyrightable design/data. **Metrics** â€” the advance table, line height, shadow rule, formatting behaviour â€” are unprotectable facts and safe to implement verbatim. Clean path: implement the metrics exactly, and hand-author your own 8x8 glyph bitmaps (or embed one of the OFL/CC0 fonts below).

## 8. Freely licensed lookalikes

| Font | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Monocraft** (IdreesInc) | SIL OFL 1.1 | Best overall match. 1500+ glyphs, explicitly clean-room: "does not include any assets or font files from the original game". Monospaced, so you lose the 1 px `i`/`l` â€” override advances yourself for vanilla rhythm. |
| **Minecraft-Font** (IdreesInc) | SIL OFL 1.1 | Proportional rendition, closer to vanilla spacing. Archived Feb 2023. Rename the family before shipping (trademark). |
| **Pixel Operator / Pixel Operator 8** (Jayvee Enaguas) | CC0 1.0 | Public domain, zero obligations â€” least legal friction of the set. 8 px raster, proportional and monospace cuts. |
| **Pixelify Sans** (Stefie Justprince) | SIL OFL 1.1 | Google Fonts + Adobe Fonts; Latin/Greek/Cyrillic; deliberately Minecraft-adjacent. |
| **Silkscreen** (Jason Kottke) | SIL OFL 1.1 | 4x5-5x5 px core; squarer and smaller than Mojangles, good for a tight UI font. |
| **Tiny5** (Stefan Schmidt) | SIL OFL 1.1 | Variable-width 5 px â€” closest in *proportional* behaviour to vanilla's variable advances. |
| **GNU Unifont** | GPLv2+ with Font Embedding Exception **and** SIL OFL 1.1 | This *is* Minecraft's Unicode fallback. Legally safe drop-in for the `uniform` font / CJK coverage. |

Avoid **Minecraftia** (Andrew Tyler, 2011) and the FontStruct "Mojangles" clones â€” freeware/personal-use, or direct traces of the proprietary design.

## 9. Hand-authoring a lookalike 5x7 / 6x8 bitmap font

Grid: **8x8 cell**, ink left-aligned from column 0, baseline after row 6, one descender row (7). Design nearly everything inside a **5 wide x 7 tall** box.

**Stroke weight: exactly 1 px, everywhere.** There is not a single 2-px stroke in the ASCII set. Never thicken anything â€” bold is generated at render time by the +1 px double-draw.

**Curves: none, but it is not strictly orthogonal either.** Two distinct construction idioms:
- **Chamfered "round" letters** (`O C G D Q S 0 8 o c e s a b d g p q u n m`): a round side is a 3-px horizontal bar inset 1 px from the stem columns, with the corner pixel simply omitted. `O` = row0 `.###.`, rows1-5 `#...#`, row6 `.###.`. That single-pixel corner notch is the entire "curve" vocabulary.
- **True 1-px diagonals** (`V W X Y Z K M N / \ % 4 7 z x v k ( ) < > { }`): stair-stepped one pixel per row. `X` steps `#...#` -> `.#.#.` -> `..#..` and mirrors.
- **`A` has no diagonal at all** â€” `.###.` apex over `#...#`, a full `#####` crossbar on row 2, then straight `#...#` legs. This flat-topped, vertical-sided `A` is one of the strongest Mojangles tells. Same story for `M` and `W`: a 2-3 row internal chevron rather than full-height diagonals (`M` = `#...#` / `##.##` / `#.#.#` / straight legs; `W` is the vertical mirror with the chevron near the bottom).

**The signature "shoulder step".** Where a bowl or shoulder joins a stem in `b d h n p q r`, Mojangles doubles the junction pixel across two rows: row2 `#.##.`, row3 `##..#`. That 2-px diagonal knee instead of a clean right angle is the single most imitable idiom in the face â€” reproduce it and text instantly reads as Minecraft.

**Requested letterforms** (5 px wide unless noted; x-height rows 2-6):
- **`a`** â€” single-storey with an *open* top-left. Row2 = 3-px bar inset 1 px; row3 = right stem only; row4 = 4-px crossbar; row5 = left stem only; row6 = 4-px bottom bar. The counter is closed only in the bottom half and the top-left corner is deliberately left open. Not the geometric double-storey `a` most pixel fonts use.
- **`g`** â€” single-storey bowl rows 2-5 (`.####` / `#...#` / `#...#` / `.####`), then the tail: row6 = right stem alone, row7 = a **4-px bar running leftwards**. The descender is a flat horizontal hook, not a curl or a straight leg.
- **`e`** â€” row2 `.###.`; row3 `#...#`; row4 is a **full-width 5-px crossbar** touching both edges (unusual); row5 = left stem alone; row6 = 4-px bottom bar shifted right. Aperture opens at bottom-right.
- **`s`** â€” pure 1-px Z-spine: row2 `.####` (top bar right-shifted), row3 left stem only, row4 `.###.` (3-px middle bar inset both sides), row5 right stem only, row6 `####.` (bottom bar left-shifted). Flat terminals, point-symmetric.
- **`t`** â€” only **3 px wide** (advance 4). Full-height 7-px stem in column 1, 3-px crossbar on row 2 (columns 0-2), and a 1-px **foot kick to the right** on row 6 (column 2). The stem itself does not reach the baseline column; the kick does.
- **`y`** â€” built as a `u` with a hook, not a diagonal `v`. Rows 2-4 `#...#`, row5 `.####`, row6 right stem alone, row7 a 4-px leftward bar â€” the identical descender hook as `g`. Reuse one tail shape for both.

**Other high-signal details:** `i` is a **single 1-px column** â€” dot row 0, empty row 1, stem rows 2-6. `l` is 2 px wide: stem rows 0-5 in column 0 plus a 1-px foot kick right on row 6, which is what distinguishes it from `I` (3 px, slab-serif `###` / `.#.` x5 / `###`). `!` has its stem on rows 0-4, a gap on row 5, dot on row 6. `:` is two pixels, rows 2 and 6. `0` carries an internal **diagonal slash** (rows 2-4 step `#..##` / `#.#.#` / `##..#`) â€” a slashed zero. `1` has a 2-px flag on row 1 and a full 5-px base serif on row 6. `9` ends in a leftward 2-px tail on row 6 rather than a straight stem. `r` is a full 5 px wide (not narrow) because its shoulder reaches column 4 on row 3. `w` ends in a 4-px bar on row 6 whereas `v` comes to a single-pixel point. `f` is 4 px wide with the top hook turning right and a 4-px crossbar on row 2. `@` is the widest glyph at 6 px ink and the only one whose ink starts on row 1.
